note: docs/design/FLOOR.md § 11's `fx-office` (card#11144, AT-D3-22): the reserved desk seats its role and nobody else. Every run is fx-snapshot-4's four `aimla` seats over the shipped default map itself (`@json:resources/floor/default.tmj`, which reserves desk id 3 — index 2 after the id sort — for `pm`), save the two runs that change the map, which carry a copy of its grid and `desks` layer (its tile layers, which no run draws, left out) changed as their notes say. Every slot is re-derived by the test from § 3.2's published function, not asserted here.

fx-office.note: AT-D3-22's GREEN: the shipped default's reservation (desk id 3, index 2, `reserved_for: pm`) over fx-snapshot-4's four seats. `aimla-pm` is the one seat relaying `pm`, so it sits at the reserved desk by its role; `aimla-impl-2` hashes to that desk and probes past it to slot 4 — § 3.2's worked table.

fx-office-none.note: Q3 A: nobody is eligible — `aimla-pm` relays `protocol_agent_role: null`, as a seat on a reporter older than card#11144 does, and a null matches no desk. The reserved desk stays empty and reserved, `aimla-pm` hashes to its own slot 0, `aimla-impl-2` still probes past the desk to 4, and § 5.5's line reads that no seat holds the role.

fx-office-first-appearance.note: § 3.4's first-appearance row, for a client holding the seat from a snapshot: `aimla-pm` is provisioned and has never reported (`offline`, `no_data_yet`, `protocol_agent_role: null`), so it is hashed to slot 0. Its first delta takes it out of `offline` (A1, at its hash slot); the role arrives on the next delta, which moves it to the reserved desk (A16, whose cause is that delta's `state_version`).

fx-office-first-appearance-insert.note: § 3.4's first-appearance row, for a client that connected before the seat was provisioned (§ 9 F8's insert): a delta names `aimla-pm`, which the client does not hold; the fetch inserts it with `protocol_agent_role: null`, so it appears at its hash slot 0 with no arrival animation; the role's delta then moves it to the reserved desk (A16, cause that delta's `state_version`).

fx-office-two.note: Q4 A: a second seat relaying `pm` arrives. `aimla-pm-2` is inserted (h mod 6 = 5, free), the reserved desk now has two eligible seats and seats neither: the incumbent `aimla-pm` walks out to its hash slot 0 (A16, cause the arriving `aimla/aimla-pm-2`), the desk stands empty, and § 9 F22's notice names both seats.

fx-office-two-relayed.note: Q4 A by a relayed role: `aimla-review`'s roster role changes to `pm` on a delta. Two seats are then eligible and neither is seated: the incumbent `aimla-pm` walks out to its hash slot 0 (A16, whose cause is `aimla-review`'s delta's `state_version`), `aimla-review` stays at its hash slot, and § 9 F22's notice names both.

fx-office-handover.note: § 3.2's handover: `fx-office-two`, then the old PM is retired. While both are present the desk seats neither (F22) and `aimla-pm` has walked out; the retirement removes `aimla-pm` (A13) and `aimla-pm-2`, now the one eligible seat, walks from slot 5 into the reserved desk (A16, cause the departed `aimla/aimla-pm`).

fx-office-grouped.note: card#11187 with card#11144: the shipped default's reserved `desks` layer moved inside a Tiled `group`. The client finds the layer at any depth, so the reservation is read there too and `aimla-pm` sits at the reserved desk exactly as on `fx-office`.

fx-office-helper.note: Q2 A: the client knows no role by name, only the equality. The shipped default, its desk id 3 reserved for `pm-helper` instead; `aimla-review` relays `pm-helper` and sits there, while `aimla-pm`, relaying `pm`, matches nothing and hashes to slot 0. A client holding a closed set of roles would leave the desk empty.
